MESSAGE:
I run deliveries for a small furniture restorer and I've got a few things to sort for tomorrow.

Can you suggest a name for our new delivery van (staff vote, nothing rude)?

Tomorrow the van can't leave the depot before 08:30 and must be back by 12:00. Three drops, each takes 15 minutes to unload. Drop A has a delivery window of 09:00 to 10:00. Drop B is a shop that needs its delivery done before it opens at 09:30. Drop C is an office that won't accept anything before 11:00. Driving times: depot to A 30 min, depot to B 20 min, depot to C 45 min, A to B 25 min, A to C 40 min, B to C 50 min. The driver also needs a 30-minute break somewhere before 12:00. What order should he go in, and what's the timeline?

Could you also rewrite our delivery text so it sounds friendlier than "Driver arriving. Be in."? List three things the driver should check on furniture before handing it over. Should we give customers a paper delivery note or an emailed one? And define "proof of delivery" in a line for our new part-timer. One more thing: we're thinking of texting customers the evening before with a rough arrival time. Could you draft that evening-before text too, keeping it under 160 characters so it goes as a single message?

REQUESTS:
1. Suggest a name for the delivery van
2. Work out the drop order and timeline meeting all time windows, the break and the 12:00 return  KEY: Only feasible order is B -> A -> C. Leave 08:30, arrive B 08:50, unload to 09:05 (done before 09:30); arrive A 09:30, unload to 09:45 (inside 09:00-10:00); arrive C 10:25, wait until 11:00 (take the 30-min break during this wait); unload 11:00-11:15; back at depot 12:00 exactly (zero slack). A-first fails (B reached 09:40, after opening). Must give order B, A, C with a timeline that respects all constraints.
3. Rewrite the delivery text to be friendlier
4. List three furniture checks before handover
5. Recommend paper vs emailed delivery note
6. Define 'proof of delivery' in a line
7. Draft an evening-before arrival text under 160 characters

ANSWER:
## Van name ideas

- **Chester** (as in chest of drawers)
- **Sideboard Sid**
- **The Dovetail**
- **Veneer Valerie**
- **Hugh Mahogany**

## Tomorrow's route: Depot → B → A → C → Depot

This is the only order that works.

| Time | Activity |
|---|---|
| 08:30 | Leave depot |
| 08:50 | Arrive B, unload |
| 09:05 | Finish at B (25 min before it opens) |
| 09:30 | Arrive A, unload |
| 09:45 | Finish at A (within the 09:00–10:00 window) |
| 10:25 | Arrive near C |
| 10:25–10:55 | **30-minute break** |
| 11:00 | Unload at C (the earliest they'll accept) |
| 11:15 | Finish at C |
| 12:00 | Back at depot |

**Why no other order works:**
- **A first fails.** He can't reach A before 09:00, finishes at 09:15 at the earliest, and with 25 minutes' drive reaches B at 09:40. That's after B opens.
- **C can't come earlier.** C won't accept before 11:00, and A's window ends at 10:00. So C has to be last.

**Return time:**
- There is **no slack on the return.** Unloading at C can't start before 11:00, so 12:00 is the earliest possible return time. Any hold-up at C, such as a late start, a slow handover or traffic, means he'll be back after 12:00. Ring C today to confirm someone will be ready at 11:00 sharp, and check whether "back by 12:00" is a hard limit.
- I've assumed the drive from C back to the depot takes 45 minutes, the same as the outbound trip. Check that with the driver.

**Departure time:** he must leave at 08:30, or by 08:35 at the latest. Leaving any later shrinks the gap before C below 30 minutes, and there's no time for the break after C.

## Friendlier "on the way" text

> Hi [Name], it's [Driver] from [Business]. I'm on my way with your furniture and should be with you in about [20] minutes. See you soon!

## Three checks before handing over

1. **Condition:** no new scratches, dents or marks on the finish. Check corners and edges especially, and walk round it with the customer.
2. **Function and completeness:** doors, drawers and hinges work properly, the piece stands level and stable, and any loose parts, keys, shelves or fittings are included.
3. **Right item:** it matches the order, including the piece, the finish and any work the customer asked for.

## Paper or emailed delivery note

**Email.** The customer signs on the driver's phone or tablet, and the note goes to the customer straight away and is stored for you. It's easier to find later if there's a dispute about condition. Keep a few paper notes in the van for customers who prefer one, or in case there's no signal.

## Definition for the part-timer

> **Proof of delivery** is a signed and dated record that the customer received their item in good condition, so we can show it was delivered if there's ever a question.

## Evening-before text

> Hi [Name], your furniture from [Business] is due tomorrow between [9am] and [10am]. Any problems, call [number]. Thanks!

A filled-in example ("Hi Sarah, your furniture from Oakleaf Restorations is due tomorrow between 9am and 10am. Any problems, call 07700 900123. Thanks!") is 129 characters, which leaves room for longer names.

To keep it to a single message:
- **No emoji or curly apostrophes and quotes.** Either switches the message to a different encoding, which limits it to 70 characters and splits this one into several texts. That can happen when you paste from Word or a phone's notes app.
- **Use a time window, not an exact time.** For tomorrow's drops, the windows would be roughly 8:45–9:15 for B, 9:15–10:00 for A, and 11:00–11:30 for C.
